Bug_Title: Nm: Class defines equal(Object); should it be equals(Object)? (NM_BAD_EQUAL)
Bug_Details:
This class defines a method equal(Object).  This method does
not override the equals(Object) method in java.lang.Object,
which is probably what was intended. equal(Object) equals(Object) java.lang.Object
Bug_Explanation: The class EqualBugExample defines a method equal(Object). However, this method does not override the equals(Object) method in java.lang.Object, as intended. The bug leads to unexpected behavior when comparing objects using the equals method.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when we compare obj1 and obj2 using the equals method. The equal method in EqualBugExample does not override the equals method in java.lang.Object, which is probably what was intended. Therefore, the equals method uses the default implementation from Object, which compares object references instead of object values. This leads to a false equality check, causing the test to fail.
